subject: Ellis Labs: hosted API budget & peak TPS — post-demo recap
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Ellis Grant <ellis.grant@ellislabs.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ellis Labs hosted API — quick follow-up and numbers we discussed

Hi Ellis / Simone / Ava,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — great questions from Ava on tokenization and prefix caching. Per our call I wanted to capture the numbers we discussed and the options that map to your target $/1M tokens. Below is a short recap and a clear set of asks so we can lock a pricing path.

Recap of what you said on the call:
- Primary usage: live chat assistant in customer-facing web app (English) + occasional background batch for analytics.
- Target monthly active users: ~120k in Q3 ramp, estimated ~40M generated tokens / month initially.
- Peak TPS window: 120 concurrent requests per second for short-chats (avg 12 tokens per response), spikes to ~250 TPS for 90s after marketing pushes.
- Budget range: internal target ~$900–1,200 per 1M generated tokens (includes inference + support SLA). You flagged unit econ sensitivity if costs exceed $1.5k/1M.

What I attached: token estimate workbook (ellislabs_token_estimate_v2.xlsx) and three pricing scenarios (low/med/high) that map to batching and quantization profiles (redwood-hosted-pricing-scenarios.pdf).

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the expected steady-state monthly token range (pick one): 20–40M, 40–80M, 80–150M?
2) For peak planning, is the 250 TPS spike a <=10 min event or sustained ~30–45 min during promos?
3) Which model tier do you expect to prioritize? (high-quality 70B, balanced 13B, low-cost 7B). This affects kernel choices and unit price.
4) Procurement: who will sign the PO? Simone — can you share the required billing contact + any procurement timing constraints?

I can turn these three scenarios into a formal quote once you confirm the bullets above. If it helps, we can lock a short-term pilot with a $X/month commit to hit predictable unit economics while you ramp.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

Attachment: ellislabs_token_estimate_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 34KB)
Attachment: redwood-hosted-pricing-scenarios.pdf (pdf, 120KB)
From: Ellis Grant <ellis.grant@ellislabs.ai>

Cc: Simone Hart <simone.hart@ellislabs.ai>, Ava R. <ava.r@ellislabs.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ellis Labs hosted API — quick follow-up and numbers we discussed

Hi Marcus — thanks for the clear follow-up. Quick answers inline: 

> 1) steady-state monthly token range
We expect to land in the 40–80M band by month 3 of launch. Early pilot is closer to 25–30M.

> 2) peak planning 250 TPS duration
Spikes are typically short — ~8–12 minutes after a push. We do have a weekly marketing digest that can push longer (~25–40 minutes) but that's predictable and we can pre-warm or schedule.

> 3) model tier priority
We want the balanced 13B for now (good latency/cost tradeoff). If quality regressions appear on high-value flows we may bump to 70B for the smaller subset of calls.

> 4) procurement
Simone here — billing contact will be procurement@ellislabs.ai, PO approvals take ~2–3 weeks. We prefer net 45 on initial contracts.

Also attaching a short internal note on tokenization assumptions (see attached).

Ellis

Folks — forwarding Ellis' confirmation. Key takeaways for quote and capacity planning:
- Steady-state: 40–80M tokens/mo (pilot 25–30M).
- Peak profile: 250 TPS spikes but typically <=12 min; weekly ~25–40 min predictable windows.
- Model: 13B mainline; 70B for a small % of calls (fallback / high-quality).
- Procurement timeline: PO + net45, 2–3 week approval.

Action items: 
- Lauren: please draft a hosted quotation with three tiers: 30M pilot band, 60M steady band, 120M uplift band. Include explicit $/1M token lines with and without auto-batching and with our recommended caching profile. Target initial sticker at $1,050/1M tokens for the 60M band with an option to add reserved throughput during promos.
- Stephanie: run a quick capacity note on how pre-warming + burst pools would be configured given the 250 TPS short spikes. Include an ops-runbook snippet we can send Ellis about pre-warm scheduling.

I'll turn the attachments into the quote once we have your numbers.

Thanks — Marcus

Thanks all — attaching a draft quote PDF (redwood-hosted-pricing-scenarios.pdf) and an annotated unit-econ table. Summary: 

- Pilot (30M tokens/mo): $1,300 per 1M tokens (pilot rate, includes onboarding & 30-day support window).
- Steady (60M tokens/mo): $1,050 per 1M tokens (targeted band you asked for).
- Uplift (120M tokens/mo): $890 per 1M tokens (committed reserved capacity).

We included a line item for reserved burst capacity to cover 250 TPS spikes for up to 45 minutes (billed as peak-hours reserve) — Simone, that can be toggled in the contract.

Ellis — if this looks reasonable I can open a DocuSign for a pilot SOW and attach the PO instructions for your procurement team.

Lauren Bishop
